Much like his grandfather,<ref name="Phantom Menace" /> Anakin revealed an incredible aptitude for machinery at age two,<ref name="Junior Jedi Knights: Lyric's World" /> surpassing his older sister Jaina;<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters" /> both Solo twins had to acknowledge their younger brother as something of a genius. Not only did this enable him to solve complex puzzles,<ref name="Junior Jedi Knights: The Golden Globe" /> but through the Force, he could look through the inner workings of machines to see whether they were functional or not, suggesting some form of [[mechu-deru]].<ref name="Ambush at Corellia" /><ref name="Junior Jedi Knights: Vader's Fortress" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Character arc===
[[File:Guide.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Anakin Solo]]
Anakin Solo was first mentioned as a nameless unborn baby of Leia Organa Solo in the [[Dark Empire 5|fifth issue]] of the [[1991]]&ndash;[[1992]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'', which was written by [[Tom Veitch]].<ref name="DE5" /> The series is set in the year 10 ABY.<ref name="NEC" /> Veitch developed Anakin because he thought Han and Leia having a child was inevitable if they got married. He was surprised when [[Timothy Zahn]]'s novel ''[[The Last Command]]'' introduced Anakin's older twin siblings Jacen and Jaina.<ref name="Veitch Interview">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarsunderworld.com/2016/08/interview-with-dark-empire-writer-tom.html|text=Interview with ''Dark Empire'' Writer Tom Veitch|work=Star Wars Underworld|archivedate=20200613234534}}</ref> Veitch also came up with naming Anakin Solo after his grandfather so he would be the embodiment of both the light and dark aspects of the Skywalker bloodline and suffer great inner conflict in his life. These characteristics, however, were largely ignored in later [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] projects which handled Anakin's character arc.<ref name="Anakin's Abandoned CA">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/star-wars-expanded-universe-was-born-eu|text=How the Star Wars Expanded Universe Was Born|date=2020-08-14|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|archivedate=20200815131840}}</ref>

Not long afterward, author [[Kevin J. Anderson]] was writing [[Star Wars: The Jedi Academy Trilogy|''The Jedi Academy Trilogy'']] of novels, set in 11 ABY, and he was informed that he needed to build upon the events of ''Dark Empire''.<ref name="Databank" /> The name "Anakin Solo" thus first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' Legends in [[1994]]'s ''[[Jedi Search]]'', the first book of Anderson's trilogy,<ref name="Jedi Search" /> and the character made his first appearance in the followup ''[[Dark Apprentice]]''.<ref name="Dark Apprentice" /> Solo went on to appear in several more novels<ref name="Champions of the Force" /><ref name="The Crystal Star" /><ref name="Ambush at Corellia" /><ref name="Children of the Jedi">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> before his birth was depicted in the [[Dark Empire II 6|sixth issue]] of Veitch's ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]'', released in [[1995]].<ref name="Dark Empire II" />

=== Death ===
During the earliest planning stage of [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] series, in a pitched outline featuring [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]-like antagonists, Anakin was outlined to be the main hero of prophecy, who would brush with the dark side before slaying Jacen in combat, after which he would eventually take up Luke's role as the leader of the Jedi Order.<ref name="Essential Reader's Companion" /> This proposal was rejected by [[George Lucas]], who felt that Anakin's trajectory followed his [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|namesake]]'s plotline in the [[prequel trilogy]] too closely; he felt it was unoriginal and repetitive, evaluating the outline as ''"too redundant to movie storylines."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1">{{YouTube|video=R19qQCyhodo|text=Crafting An Epic: The Making of the New Jedi Order &#124; Part I: Creation &#124; Star Wars Documentary|channel=@holonetwork|name=holonet|date=2025-01-08}}</ref> He encouraged the team to ''"be more original"'' with the ''New Jedi Order'' storyline and to create a more compelling antagonist and story arc -- it was at this point that [[James Luceno]] was invited onto the project to help draft a new outline. This feedback from Lucas, and the decision stemming from it, was made in [[May]] [[1998]], during the story planning, over a year before the series would publish its first novel.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" />

While Lucas had told the story team to ''"change person who is responsible for ultimately saving the day to Jacen -- not Anakin,"''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" /> [[Lucas Licensing|Lucasfilm]] editor [[Sue Rostoni]] would clarify that ''"George did not tell us to kill Anakin. He didn't tell us to kill anybody. He approved the deaths of characters, in theory, then told us who we couldn't kill."''<ref name="draft2">"[George Lucas is] the one who said that the alien invaders could not be dark-side Force-users, that we couldn't kill Luke, that we had to kill Anakin instead of Jacen*(we originally had planned it the other way around)."<br />"His objection to Anakin Solo being the main series protagonist was, I think, possible confusion with Anakin Skywalker in the prequel trilogy of movies&#x2026;Anakin was our first choice as the saga's hero, not Jacen. When George nixed that idea, we were forced to rethink everything very quickly, as the first book of the series was already being outlined."<br />&#x2014;[[Shelly Shapiro]] and [[James Luceno]] from the "[[Star Wars: New Jedi Order Round-Robin Interview]]"<br /><div class="references-small">Later, Shelly Shapiro clarified in the VIP thread in the official site that "Actually I don't really know what happened, I thought Lucas was involved but I'm not sure, what I said was just speculation based on what I thought I knew." Sue Rostini also stated that George Lucas did not order Anakin to be killed off. "No, George did not tell us to kill Anakin. He didn't tell us to kill anybody. He approved the deaths of characters, in theory, then told us who we COULDN'T kill (i.e., Luke). The creative group decided the main story plot points (i.e., the deaths) and the author(s) created the action and situations."</div></ref> With a new outline worked out, and a new [[Yuuzhan Vong empire|villain]] created, the story team decided that with Jacen as the hero of the series, Anakin would fall in combat during the course of the war,<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" /> with the latter's death scheduled to appear in ''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''.<ref name="draft1">[[Jason Fry|Fry Jacen]], "[[The New Jedi Order in 100 Easy Lessons]]," [[Star Wars Insider 74|''Star Wars Insider'' 74]], March/April 2004.</ref> 

[[File:Agentsofchaosanakin.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Anakin Solo on the cover of ''Agents of Chaos'']]
Though the NJO story team largely agreed it was important to have a Solo child die midway through the series, series consultant [[Michael A. Stackpole]] objected; he stated that he thought the decision to kill off Anakin was ''"a waste of character... I felt there was more we could do with him."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" /> Fellow series consultant James Luceno recalled this discussion in the NJO writers' room, saying that, ''"I do remember that... We all had to sort of gang up on Mike. He was pushing back."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" /> Despite Stackpole's disagreement, the NJO story team agreed to go forward with the plan; still resolute, Stackpole said that his strong characterization of Anakin when writing the [[Dark Tide duology|''Dark Tide'' duology]] was partly due to the fact that he was ''"hoping, hoping, hoping that maybe somebody would decide that he'd get a reprieve."''<ref name="Stackpole">Erik. ''[http://theforce.net/podcast/story/Podcast_Michael_Stackpole_Interview_Part_2_93953.asp Interview with Michael Stackpole (Part 2)]''. theForce.Net ([[2005]]-[[2005#July|07-27]]).<br />"There was some original design ideas that we had and certain timing issues; certain events that we thought should happen later or earlier in the series that didn't. You know, one of things that was decided above my paygrade and that I ''never'' liked was [Anakin Solo] dying. I personally thought that it was a waste of character, and this is part of the reason why I characterized him as much, and did as much with him, as I did in the two books I did in NJO, 'cause I was hoping, hoping, ''hoping'' that maybe somebody would decide that he'd get a reprieve. Alas&hellip;"<br />&mdash;[[Michael A. Stackpole]]</ref> Privately, Stackpole had envisioned a possible future for Anakin as a Jedi leading a rag-tag group of heroes around the galaxy doing good deeds,<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4">{{YouTube|video=BOa1MEJVOig|text=Crafting An Epic: The Making of the New Jedi Order &#124; Part IV: Abyss &#124; Star Wars Documentary|channel=@holonetwork|name=holonet|date=2025-02-01}}</ref> not unlike what [[Greg Keyes]] would choose to do with rescue pilot [[Uldir Lochett]] and Jedi [[Klin-Fa Gi]] in the series' own ''[[Emissary of the Void]]''.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 3">{{YouTube|video=AiNTRIfprJQ|text=Crafting An Epic: The Making of the New Jedi Order &#124; Part III: Recoil &#124; Star Wars Documentary|channel=@holonetwork|name=holonet|date=2025-01-20}}</ref>

Following ''Dark Tide'', the story outline continued as planned, with one major change: the ''[[Knightfall Trilogy]]'', starring [[Danni Quee]], was cancelled (even after the first book, [[The New Jedi Order: Knightfall I: Jedi Storm|''Jedi Storm'']], was finished) in favor of its replacement, the [[Edge of Victory Duology|''Edge of Victory'' duology]]. This was done to feature Anakin more prominently before his death. [[Del Rey]] editor [[Shelly Shapiro]] remarked about the decision, ''"When we had to kill Anakin, everyone sat around saying, 'Well, Anakin isn't much of a character. Who's going to care?' So we made a point of building him up in the books until then,"'' adding that she felt it worked, saying, ''"Then he dies, and the outcry was, 'How could you do this?!' So I call that success, I think we did it right. We made it an important death."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4" /> [[Troy Denning]], who wrote Anakin Solo's death in ''Star by Star'', recalled in [[2009]] that it had taken him around seven drafts to pen the scene,<ref name="Tailone fights">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29969473|board=Literature|thread=The exquisite art of fight writing! How do you do it??|user=Tailone|date=2009-04-17|time=12:34 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200419100449/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-exquisite-art-of-fight-writing-how-do-you-do-it.29961053}}</ref> adding that he saved writing Leia's reaction to the news for last, knowing he would inevitably be emotional writing it.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4" />

As was planned from the beginning, the death of Anakin would shape the rest of the series, strongly affecting the character development of Jaina and Jacen for the following books of the ''New Jedi Order'' series.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" /> [[Walter Jon Williams]], author of ''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way|Destiny's Way]]'', elaborated on the element of surprise with the death, saying, "''Readers were meant to be led to the conclusion that Anakin was going to be the big hero of the series. But he died -- and he'll stay that way,"'' adding that while Anakin's role was important, ''"his interpretation of the Force was incomplete."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4" /> ''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Journey|Dark Journey]]'' author [[Elaine Cunningham]] viewed the death of Anakin as of historic importance in the universe, comparing his demise to that of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Frederick,_Prince_of_Wales Prince Henry Frederick], saying, ''"Here's someone who showed enormous potential. [Like] a Prince of England who died at the age of 18 -- he would have been an exceptional ruler. That always seemed like promise that was just wasted. And Anakin obviously was exceptional."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4" />

On the importance of Anakin's death to the storyline, Luceno shared, ''"You want those moments in fiction, you know, that are going to affect readers and get them more invested. It made sense because we're going to elevate another person. This is typical mythology, where a figure of power dies so another person can ascend."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 1" /> Author [[Matthew Stover]] would add, ''"If you didn't know Anakin and watch what happened to him in Star by Star, if you didn't know that, you don't know where Jacen is at the beginning of [<nowiki/>[[The New Jedi Order: Traitor|Traitor]]]. I feel like without that context, it's not really that powerful a story."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 5">{{YouTube|video=VltR6kIQa7A|text=Crafting An Epic: The Making of the New Jedi Order &#124; Part V: Satori &#124; Star Wars Documentary|channel=@holonetwork|name=holonet|date=2025-04-23}}</ref>

In multiple polls taken throughout and after the series, ''New Jedi Order'' readers felt that Anakin's death was the most impactful death of the series. In [[March]] [[2003]], 52% of readers missed Anakin the most, compared to only 33.5% for Chewbacca.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4" /> Two years later, in late [[2005]], 45% of readers rated Anakin's death as the most unexpected death of the series, compared to 31% for Chewbacca, along with 8% for [[Borsk Fey'lya]] and 7% for [[Vergere]], respectively. Readers also rated Anakin's death as the most meaningful of the series.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 7">{{YouTube|video=5wzjFPNTznU|text=Crafting An Epic: The Making of the New Jedi Order &#124; Part VII: Unification &#124; Star Wars Documentary|channel=@holonetwork|name=holonet|date=2025-07-27}}</ref> Luceno recalled that there was not as prominent a public backlash to the death as there was with ''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime|Vector Prime]]'', saying, ''"It was not like it was with Chewbacca. People were along for the ride by then."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 4" />  

''[[Force Heretic trilogy|Force Heretic]]'' author [[Sean Williams]] rated Anakin's death as the ''"most emotional moment for me in that series,"'' adding, ''"It was such an amazing moment. It was very moving, very powerful. And the whole book kind of worked up to this huge conclusion and it was fantastic. It had that sucker punch feeling."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 6">{{YouTube|video=bZH-dlqQq-8|text=Crafting An Epic: The Making of the New Jedi Order &#124; Part VI: Anabasis &#124; Star Wars Documentary|channel=@holonetwork|name=holonet|date=2025-03-20}}</ref> Luceno would additionally comment, ''"It was good because those sorts of deaths upset people because they no longer know which way the series is going to go -- anyone is up for grabs now, anything could happen. And that's always good, that kind of tension."''<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 7" />

By the end of the series, in a 2005 poll of over a thousand readers, Anakin would rank as the second most popular male character of the ''New Jedi Order'' series, with 25% of the vote, behind Jacen with 38%.<ref name="NJO Documentary Pt. 7" />

=== Later proposal ===
For ''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]'', the ninth and final volume of the [[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force|''Legacy of the Force'']] series, Denning proposed an ending that would have resurrected Anakin by having Jacen flow-walking back to the moment Anakin was killed to corrupt Tahiri into becoming his apprentice, only to make contact and switch places with Anakin, leading Jacen's body to be disguised as if it were Anakin's to not alter the past and Anakin's corpse to be brought back to the present and resurrected by Jaina. However, Denning's proposal was not explored despite being suggested in the outline.<ref name="Essential Reader's Companion">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref>

===Prophecies===
There are several prophecies about Anakin that never took place because of his death. In ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]'', Luke had a vision of Anakin and his siblings leading the Jedi Order.<ref name="Dark Empire II" /> Likewise, in ''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory I: Conquest]]'', Ikrit told Anakin that there would be something great born in him and Tahiri.<ref name="Edge of Victory I: Conquest" /> Tom Veitch stated that his original plan for Anakin's story arc was to follow him on his inner struggles to control the light and dark sides until the former eventually won, yet subsequent Legends writers opted to constantly focus on Anakin's light side and kill him off heroically. While Veitch had nothing against their decisions, he felt a certain amount of regret that many stories focusing on Anakin's inner conflict were never told.<ref name="Anakin's Abandoned CA" />
